blocks.text: PAGADIAN CITY, Zamboanga del Sur — Aiming to enrich Mindanao’s history, scholar and ethnographer Dr. Wendell Glenn Cagape launched his new book, “Colonial Images of the Subano Nation,” here on Sunday. The historical and ethnographic work explores the colonial history, cultural resilience and identity of the Subanen Indigenous people across the Zamboanga Peninsula. By examining the Jesuit colonial project, along with the dynamics of Indigenous resistance and cooperation, Cagape reclaims historical archives, early maps and colonial photographs through a decolonial lens to highlight the enduring heritage of the Subanen, the largest Indigenous population in the Philippines.
